ai.description: Cnemaspis agarwali reaches a snout-vent length of 35 mm. It is brown with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and dark lateral blotches. Key features include a granular dorsum and smooth ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis agarwali* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its throat, which is absent in most other similar Indian species.
ai.habitat: Agarwal’s Dwarf Gecko inhabits moist deciduous forests in the northern Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks and rocky outcrops at elevations between 500 and 800 meters.
ai.behavior: Agarwal’s dwarf gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its rocky forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis agarwali* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Cnemaspis agarwali is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, specifically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
